narrative: Five routine admin/access tickets over four months, all closed fast (2-9 days). The one recurring issue is alert emails going to spam: the follow-up ticket says the fix from last month is 'mostly fixed but about one in five emails still gets flagged,' with no later ticket confirming full resolution. Otherwise calm, transactional traffic (password reset, role change, auditor dashboard sharing) - healthy account, just confirm the spam fix actually closed the loop.

High-volume account (16 tickets, Dec 2024-Oct 2025) with a recurring pattern: connector, report builder, dashboard, API and alert failures that get fixed in 1-2 days but keep recurring in slightly different guises - 'Yesterday's fix didn't hold,' 'the same blank-tile issue from February is back,' 'Second day in a row.' By October 2025 the tone has hardened into dry fatalism ('At this point we could set our calendar by these outages'), and the account still runs a routine renewal/seat-count check in between, so it's engaged but structurally unstable rather than leaving. Alert coverage is a specific sore point - alerts twice failed to fire on real outages ('What's the point of the alert module if it goes quiet exactly when we need it?').

Textbook recovery arc: a data-warehouse connector outage sat unresolved for months (Dec 2024-Apr 2025) while support 'bounced this between two teams,' prompting a formal escalation demanding 'a named technical contact and a fix timeline, not another ticket in the queue.' After the root-cause writeup in July 2025 the account visibly calms down - 'Confirming dashboards have been running clean for a week... good to finally see this closed out properly' - followed by cheerful feature requests and a new-connector onboarding ask in October. One trivial cosmetic issue (alert digest rendering in Outlook) is still open but explicitly 'not urgent.'

Light, low-drama traffic centred on integrating Kataja with an accounting system (API keys, sync frequency, export formatting). The one open item - custom column ordering for exports - is a plain feature request with no urgency language and no follow-up chasing. Nothing here reads as risk.

Four tickets in three months, all routine board-meeting logistics (dashboard restore, seat provisioning, alert recipient updates, renewal seat audit). No friction, no repeat issues, no negative language anywhere - a quiet, healthy account.

Enterprise account with a full year of near-constant firefighting - connector, API, export, report-builder and seat incidents that repeatedly cluster on the same day or the day after each other ('On top of the API issue - the ERP connector just failed as well'). One ticket flags this explicitly: 'we've had more incidents on this account this year than I'd expect at our tier,' and an earlier one demands 'please escalate internally, this is an Enterprise account.' Despite the volume nothing recurs verbatim without eventual acknowledgment of a fix, but the underlying reliability problem (especially connector drops and alerts that miss real failures) is never shown to be actually solved rather than repeatedly patched.

Three tickets in five months, all straightforward how-to and configuration questions (export permissions, alert setup, dashboard layout). No complaints, no recurring problems - healthy, low-touch account.

A cluster of same-day cascading failures across seats, dashboards, report builder, API and alerts from October 2024 to June 2025, capped by a partially-failed fix ('Yesterday's seat fix only partially worked, the same user still can't edit shared dashboards') and an alert-reliability problem that recurs despite a prior 'fix' ('still not catching sync failures even after last week's fix attempt. What actually changed?'). The account's last ticket in this record is a blunt, tired plea rather than a specific bug report - 'Please just get this account stable again' - which reads as patience running out with the platform as a whole, not just individual incidents.
Single ticket, one dashboard drill-down bug, resolved in four days. No history to judge a trend from, but nothing concerning in what's here.

Sparse, mixed traffic over a year: an alert formatting bug, a new connector setup, an alert-scheduling tweak, and one still-open minor gap (no way to duplicate a report template) that was never chased after the initial ticket. Tone throughout is neutral and informational - no anger, no repetition of unfixed problems.

Two tickets, five months apart, both forward-looking onboarding/configuration questions (SSO provisioning for a new department, SFTP export destination) from a named contact. Reads as an account actively expanding its use of the platform, not one with problems.

Three well-spaced, purely operational tickets over eight months (sandbox API access, incremental sync for a large table, an offboarding checklist) from one consistent contact. All resolved, none reference a recurring problem - healthy, low-touch account.

Light traffic building toward expansion: after a couple of ordinary export/connector requests in 2024, the account onboards a Nordic subsidiary's ERP as a new connector, then a year later comes back to extend dashboard access to that subsidiary's local team. No unresolved threads, no negative language - a growing footprint inside the account.

The heaviest, most chronically unstable account in the batch - 19 tickets across a year with alerts, seats, report builder, dashboards, API and connectors all failing and re-failing in tight clusters. The alert module is the specific unresolved thread: it goes silent repeatedly despite repeated 'fixes' ('Whatever the actual root cause is, patching it each time isn't working for us' in November 2024; 'Third message today. Need someone to actually look at this, not just restart it' as the final ticket in October 2025). Frustration visibly builds rather than resolves across the year, and the account ends this record on an unresolved, exasperated note with no confirmation of a fix - this needs a human CSM conversation, not another ticket close.

competitor_mentions.quote: We looked at Dashlume last year partly on speed, so this is the kind of thing that gets noticed internally.

narrative: Sparse but telling: five tickets over five months where problems get patched but not really fixed. The export-formatting ticket reveals a quiet workaround already in place - 'The team's been rebuilding the formatting in Excel afterwards for now' - and the final ticket, an API rate-limit discrepancy, is still open with 'still waiting to hear back on what's actually going on here.' A dashboard-speed complaint mentions in passing that they 'looked at Dashlume last year partly on speed,' a casual competitor reference but one raised specifically while complaining about the thing that drove the earlier evaluation. Low volume, patient tone, but the accumulation-without-resolution pattern here is a real watch flag.

Three tickets spread across sixteen months, each a distinct minor bug (formatting not saving, a documentation mismatch, a reset recipient list), all resolved within days and none referencing a prior unresolved problem. Calm, low-friction account.

A single recurring fault - the ERP connector times out intermittently - resurfaces three times over two years (mid-2024, late 2024, mid-2025), each time fixed quickly but never actually eliminated. The customer's own framing in the most recent ticket is telling: 'same pattern as last year... just noting it keeps recurring' - patient, unbothered tone, but this is exactly the kind of quiet, never-fully-fixed issue worth a proactive root-cause conversation before patience runs out.

A serious episode in the first half of the record - chronic connector and report-builder failures left unresolved for weeks, an explicit statement that 'we are reviewing whether the platform is fit for what we need,' and a formal escalation request for someone senior - is followed by genuine recovery. From August 2025 the customer volunteers positive feedback unprompted ('appreciate how much quieter things have been since the spring'; 'otherwise things have been solid'; 'support turned this around fast, good to see'). This is the improving arc: real crisis, real fix, and the customer noticing and saying so. One minor filter-persistence bug remains open but is explicitly framed as low-priority.

competitor_mentions.quote: we had another vendor pitch Dashlume to us this autumn and passed again, just wanted you to know the alerting fix from last year has held up well

narrative: Only two tickets in a year, and the second one is close to unprompted praise: after reassigning seats, the customer volunteers that 'we had another vendor pitch Dashlume to us this autumn and passed again, just wanted you to know the alerting fix from last year has held up well.' That's a real competitor evaluation event (a vendor pitch) but the account chose to stay and said so proactively - about as strong a loyalty signal as text data gets.

A rough six months in 2024 (May-October) with cascading, same-day failures across report builder, API, dashboards, alerts and exports - three separate dashboard problems in one week alone - followed by a long quiet stretch and just one ticket in 2025, a recurring blank-export problem ('Export came back completely blank again this morning'). The sharp drop in frequency after 2024 reads as improving, but that last ticket shows the export-reliability issue was never conclusively closed out, so it's worth a check that it actually stayed fixed.
